item.title: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment.…
item.description:
“But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. Udāyi, I say: ‘This person is not bound, not fettered.’ Why is that? Udāyi, the difference in his faculties has been fully understood by me.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 66 – Laṭukikopamasutta

item.title: “Here, good sirs, greed is an unwholesome state, and ill-will is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons…
item.description:
“Here, good sirs, greed is an unwholesome state, and ill-will is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons ill-will, giving rise to (pure) vision, giving rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna. And what, good sirs, is that Middle Way that gives rise to vision, gives rise to knowledge, leads to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration. This, good sirs, is the Middle Way that gives rise to vision, gives rise to knowledge, leads to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 3 – Dhammadāyādasutta

item.title: “Monks, if there were no gratification in the world, beings would not become lustful for the world. But because there is gratification in the world,…
item.description:
“Monks, if there were no gratification in the world, beings would not become lustful for the world. But because there is gratification in the world, beings become lustful for the world. If there were no peril in the world, beings would not become disenchanted with the world. But because there is peril in the world, beings become disenchanted with the world. If there were no escape from the world, beings would not escape from the world. But because there is escape from the world, beings escape from the world.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.105

item.title: Another Elder Nun Dhīrā: Dhīrā, be steadfast, Hold fast to wholesome states. O nun, with faculties developed, Bear this last body, Having conquered the forces…
item.description:
Another Elder Nun Dhīrā:

Dhīrā, be steadfast,
Hold fast to wholesome states.
O nun, with faculties developed,
Bear this last body,
Having conquered the forces of Māra’s army,
Having conquered Māra with his army.

From: Therīgāthā 1.7

item.title: “Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained…
item.description:
“Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. These six sense bases, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.94

item.title: “Truly, brahmins, this world is led by aging, illness, and death. Since the world is led by aging, illness, and death, brahmins, restraint of body,…
item.description:
“Truly, brahmins, this world is led by aging, illness, and death. Since the world is led by aging, illness, and death, brahmins, restraint of body, speech, and mind in this life is a refuge, a cave, an island (or a lamp), a shelter, and a destination for one who has gone to death.

When a house is on fire,
The goods that are removed
Are useful to the owners,
Not those burned inside.
So too, the world is burning
With aging and death on fire —
Save yourself by giving,
For what is given is well-saved.
Here, restraint of body,
Restraint of speech and mind —
One who does this, even while dying,
Experiences happiness,
Because while still alive,
He has made merit.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.52
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “One who avoids sensual desires As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head — That mindful one transcends This attachment in the world. Whoever is greedy…
item.description:
“One who avoids sensual desires
As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one transcends
This attachment in the world.

Whoever is greedy for sensual pleasures —
Land, gold, cows, horses,
Servants, attendants, women, relatives —

Weak, overcome by sensual pleasures,
Calamity crushes him,
Suffering follows him
As water rushes into a broken boat.

Therefore, always mindful,
One should abandon sensual pleasures.
Having abandoned them, one crosses the flood,
Having bailed out the boat, one reaches the far shore.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “What do you think, prince? For that householder or householder’s son, do bodily or mental fevers arise due to craving? Burned by those fevers born…
item.description:
“What do you think, prince? For that householder or householder’s son, do bodily or mental fevers arise due to craving? Burned by those fevers born of craving, does he experience suffering?” - “Yes, venerable sir.” - “That householder or householder’s son, prince, burned by fevers born of craving, experiences suffering. That craving has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, unable to arise in the future. Therefore I feel at ease.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.35
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties, virtue is destroyed. With no virtue, with deficiency in virtue, right concentration is destroyed. With…
item.description:
“Monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties, virtue is destroyed. With no virtue, with deficiency in virtue, right concentration is destroyed. With no right concentration, with deficiency in right concentration, true knowledge and vision are destroyed. With no true knowledge and vision, with deficiency in true knowledge and vision, disenchantment and dispassion are destroyed. With no disenchantment and dispassion, with deficiency in disenchantment and dispassion, the knowledge and vision of liberation are destroyed. Just as, monks, a tree with deficient branches and foliage — its shoots do not reach perfection, its bark does not reach perfection, its sapwood does not reach perfection, its heartwood does not reach perfection. So too, monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties … the knowledge and vision of liberation are destroyed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.50

item.title: “Fletchers make arrows, Potters make pots, Carpenters shape wood, The wise tame themselves.” “Like a solid rock Unmoved by the wind, So the wise are…
item.description:
“Fletchers make arrows,
Potters make pots,
Carpenters shape wood,
The wise tame themselves.”

“Like a solid rock
Unmoved by the wind,
So the wise are unmoved
Amid praise and blame.”

“Like a deep lake,
Clear, unruffled,
So the wise become serene,
Hearing the Dhamma.”

“The good renounce everything,
The virtuous do not prattle about sensual desires.
Whether touched by pleasure or pain,
The wise show neither elation nor depression.”

From: Dhammapada 76-89
